subject: MAP: performance benchmark validation & methodology triage
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@snowpeak.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — perf targets & dataset

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To summarize Snowpeak's ask for the MAP: we need a reproducible performance evaluation of Redwood's inference for our 13B decoder variant on our real prompts. Key acceptance criteria we discussed: p95 token latency < 300ms at steady-state, throughput >= 40 tokens/sec per GPU under our batching/concurrency profile, TTFT (time-to-first-token) < 120ms for streaming responses, and stable behavior up to 32 concurrent streams.

We attached a representative prompt set (snowpeak_prompt_set_v1.json) and two example request traces. Please confirm the methodology you plan to run so we can align — specifically: model checkpoint name, exact tokenization, whether server or client TTFT will be measured, warm-up duration, and the load tool you'll use. We also want a short matrix in the MAP showing what would cause us to accept vs. require follow-up work (e.g., quantization mismatch, batching differences, streaming framing).

We aim to close procurement by 2026-03-20; can Redwood run an initial pass this week and then a validation run next week?

Thanks,
Elena Novak
Head of ML Engineering, Snowpeak Analytics
elena.novak@snowpeak.ai

Attachments: snowpeak_prompt_set_v1.json (200 prompts), example_request_trace_01.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf targets & dataset

Elena / Aaron,

Appreciate the clear acceptance criteria — this is exactly what we need to close the MAP. Proposed benchmark plan (short):

1) Scope: 13B decoder variant (redwood-13b-v1) using Snowpeak prompt set (attached).
2) Measurement: server-side timestamps for TTFT + client-side hooks to verify streaming timing. Report p50/p95/p99 token latencies, aggregate tokens/sec, and end-to-end response time.
3) Environment: Redwood hosted Dedicated cluster (A100-equivalent), single-GPU baseline and 2-GPU scale test. We'll record model quantization (fp16 vs int8) and kernel selection.
4) Methodology details to confirm with you: exact tokenizer (BPE spec/version), whether you expect prefix KV caching between requests, and allowed batching window (ms).
5) Warm-up: 15–30 minutes (we recommend 30m) to reach steady-state.
6) Tools: we'll run our internal harness (perf-harness.zip) and reproduce with wrk-compatible driver you can run. We'll provide a shell script to reproduce.

Timeline: initial baseline run by 2026-03-05, deep triage & alignment 2026-03-06—03-09, validation replay 2026-03-11—03-12. That lands us to finalize MAP artifacts by 2026-03-13 if all goes well.

I've attached a MAP draft (map_draft_rishi_v1.docx) that includes an acceptance matrix and responsibilities. If you confirm tokenizer and KV expectations by EOD tomorrow we'll run the baseline.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Snowpeak MAP — repro & triage request

Team,

Looping you in to run the baseline and help triage methodology differences (Snowpeak wants the MAP by mid-March). Notes from client: they measure TTFT client-side and reported p95 ~260ms at concurrency 16. Our internal baseline historically reports p95 ~350—400ms under similar load; we need to find delta reasons.

Immediate asks:
- Laura: please run the baseline using the attached prompt set and the perf-harness instructions. Configs to run: (A) baseline single-GPU, streaming enabled, batch_window=10ms; (B) single-GPU, no-KV, batch_window=50ms; (C) int8 quant vs fp16.
- Monica: capture both server-side and client-side TTFT timestamps so we can compare measurement definitions.
- Priyom: pull the competitor config (CloudAI Inc.) we used in the previous RFP so we can replicate their harness differences.

Potential discrepancy sources to check (non-exhaustive): tokenization differences (BPE vocab mapping), streaming framing (small-chunk streaming vs buffer-then-send), batching window and owner of batching (client vs server), quantization/ops (int8 reduced kernel paths), and network path (client-side proxies).

Please drop preliminary logs to this thread by 2026-03-05 EOD. I'll summarize for Elena once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-05T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Snowpeak MAP — repro & triage request

Rishi — ran the three baseline configs you requested (attached run logs). High-level findings:

1) Quick numbers (single A100-equivalent GPU, 512-token context, steady-state after 30m warm-up):
   - Config A (streaming, batch_window=10ms, fp16): p50=80ms, p95=380ms, p99=620ms, tokens/sec=46
   - Config B (no-KV, batch_window=50ms, fp16): p50=110ms, p95=540ms, p99=900ms, tokens/sec=51
   - Config C (streaming, batch_window=10ms, int8): p50=70ms, p95=310ms, p99=580ms, tokens/sec=55

2) Repro vs Snowpeak reported p95 260ms at concurrency 16: we observe ~380ms in our streaming/fp16 baseline. Two probable contributors:
   - Quantization: when we enable int8 we close a lot of the gap (p95 drops from 380->310). Need to confirm Snowpeak used an int8-style model or a different kernel/mesa.
   - Measurement definition: Snowpeak measures TTFT strictly from client-side first byte; our server-side p95 includes tokenization + scheduling latency before the first token is flushed. When we instrumented client-side hooks the TTFT numbers dropped ~30—40ms.

3) Other notes: CloudAI's harness uses a synthetic short prompt set that favors small-decoding windows; their reported numbers matched Snowpeak's public claims but were not on the same prompt distribution. Also they used a warm-up of ~5 minutes which can under-report steady-state p95.

Next steps (proposed):
- Re-run with the exact Snowpeak tokenizer mapping (they confirmed a custom BPE patch) and int8 quant profile; reproduce with client-side measurement hooks enabled.
- Share a small test script Snowpeak can run locally to validate we’re measuring the same TTFT definition.
- Update MAP acceptance matrix to include quantization and measurement method as explicit acceptance criteria.

Dropping run artifacts: baseline_runlog_20260305.csv (summary), kernel_selection.txt (notes), quick_plots.png.

—Laura
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: MAP update: benchmarking results, methodology alignment, and next steps

Elena / Aaron — quick status update and summary of the MAP work we completed this past week. Thanks for the prompt tokenizer patch and confirmation on quantization profile — that unlocked the most important delta.

What we did:
- Matched Snowpeak's tokenizer (custom BPE patch) and ran the perf-harness with streaming small-chunk framing.
- Enabled the int8 quantization profile you indicated (we used the same checkpoint conversion flags).
- Instrumented both server-side and client-side TTFT hooks and validated timestamps against your local runs.

Key results (single GPU, 512 tokens, steady-state after 30m warm-up):
- Matched configuration: redwood-13b-v1 (int8), streaming small-chunk framing, batch_window=10ms, concurrency=16
- Measured: p50=72ms, p95=285ms, p99=510ms, tokens/sec=53, TTFT_client_side=110ms
- Reproduction variance: our numbers are within ~10% of your reported metrics; the remaining gap is explained by a small difference in client network stack (your deployment includes an edge proxy that aggregates first-chunk flushes).

Methodology alignments made:
- Explicitly agreed on tokenizer version and patch.
- TTFT definition: client-side first-byte timestamp (this is now the MAP acceptance metric).
- Warm-up: 30 minutes minimum for steady-state measurements.
- Quantization: acceptance requires a documented int8 conversion pipeline and test artifacts.

Triage notes (why initial numbers differed):
- Measurement definition mismatch (server vs client TTFT) accounted for ~30—40ms.
- Quantization/kernel path: int8 closed most of the p95 gap.
- Batching window: larger windows increased throughput but raised p95; we optimized batch_window=10ms for Snowpeak workload.

MAP next steps and asks
- I'll attach the final perf summary and updated MAP (updated_map_SP-042.xlsx, final_perf_summary.pdf). Please review the acceptance checklist and confirm you are comfortable moving to procurement.
- Proposed close date: 2026-03-18 (procurement/PO in place) — can Snowpeak confirm that target?

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through of the reproducibility report and scripts.

Thanks — great collaboration.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
